Number of decimal places in the source values

Source: R/precision.R
source_decimals.Rd

source_decimals() returns the largest number of decimal places that the non-missing values of x actually use, e.g. c(4.5, 4.25, 7) has two. It is meant to be computed on the raw analysis values (e.g. AVAL of one lab parameter, across all treatment arms and visits) so that summary statistics can be shown with a precision relative to the source data.

Usage

source_decimals(x, max_dec = 4L)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector. Non-finite values are ignored.

max_dec

Largest number of decimals to report. Defaults to 4.

Value

A single integer, 0 when there is no finite value.

Details

Numeric data does not keep trailing zeros (4.50 is stored as 4.5), so the result is the precision found in the data and can understate the precision of the collected values if no value shows a trailing zero. Binary noise (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2) is ignored. At most max_dec decimals are reported, which stops derived values such as a calculated BMI from producing very long numbers.

Examples

source_decimals(c(4.5, 4.25, 7))
#> [1] 2
source_decimals(c(30, 35, NA))
#> [1] 0
source_decimals(c(0.1 + 0.2, 1))
#> [1] 1
